# Introduction

This file is used to conduct ordinal regression analysis on the survey responses of Recreational fishers from the SELTMP in 2025. Regressions test trends between support for MPAs against responses to other survey questions and demographics
Ordinal regression workflow for survey response data
Outcome: ordered survey item (e.g., 1:10)
Predictor(s): education or demographics

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# R Setup & housekeeping
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
	echo = TRUE,
	include = TRUE,
	message = FALSE,
	warning = FALSE)

rm(list=ls())
objects()
```

```{r}
# Packages
library(tidyverse)
library(ordinal)   # clm(), nominal_test()
library(MASS)      # polr() if using Brant
library(brant)     # Brant test for proportional odds
library(car)       # optional, for model comparisons and diagnostics
library(emmeans)   # optional, for marginal means if needed
```

# 1. Prepare data
```{r}
# Import Raw Data sheet
raw_data <- read_excel(here::here("Data/SELTMP-2025-GBR-surveydataset_v1-0_RecFishingCLUSTERS_RyanW-Sept-22-2026.xlsx"), sheet = "Raw_Data")

##glimpse(raw_data)
```

```{r}
# Filter Data for only Rec Fishers
fisher_data <- raw_data |>
  filter(!is.na(inter_zoning), Are_you_a_Rec_Fisher == "Y")
```

```{r}
# Set up variables as factors 
"dat <- fisher_data %>%
  transmute(
    inter_zoning = as.integer(inter_zoning),
    educ = as.integer(educ)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(inter_zoning), !is.na(educ)) %>%
  mutate(
    inter_zoning = factor(inter_zoning, ordered = TRUE, levels = 1:10),
    educ = factor(educ, ordered = FALSE))"

# Switch education to numeric:
 dat <- dat %>% mutate(educ = as.numeric(as.character(educ)))

# Check response distribution
table(dat$inter_zoning)
```

# 2. Ordered logit model (proportional odds model)

```{r}
# Model 1: education as a single predictor

# For categorical education:
#m_ord <- clm(inter_zoning ~ educ, data = dat, link = "logit")

# For a numeric education:
 m_ord <- clm(inter_zoning ~ educ, data = dat, link = "logit")

summary(m_ord)

# To examine multiple predictors:
# m_ord_full <- clm(inter_zoning ~ educ + age_group + gender, data = dat, link = "logit")
# summary(m_ord_full)
```

# 3. Check proportional odds / parallel slopes assumption
```{r}
# Option A: nominal_test() from ordinal package
# This is a standard check for parallel slopes in clm()
nominal_test(m_ord)

# If it is significant, the proportional odds assumption is likely violated.

# Option B: Brant test (if using MASS::polr)
# This is often used when fitting a standard ordered logit/proportional odds model
# in a more classical framework.
m_p <- MASS::polr(inter_zoning ~ educ, data = dat, Hess = TRUE)
brant(m_p)

# Note:
# - If you use clm(), the nominal_test() is usually the better direct check.
# - If you use polr(), brant() is a common choice.
```



# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. LR test for overall model significance
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Null model: intercept only
m_null <- clm(inter_zoning ~ 1, data = dat, link = "logit")

# Log-likelihoods
ll_null <- as.numeric(logLik(m_null))
ll_model <- as.numeric(logLik(m_ord))

# LR statistic
lr_stat <- 2 * (ll_model - ll_null)

# Degrees of freedom difference
df_diff <- attr(logLik(m_ord), "df") - attr(logLik(m_null), "df")

# p-value
p_value <- pchisq(lr_stat, df = df_diff, lower.tail = FALSE)

# Report
data.frame(
  Model = "Ordered logit vs intercept only",
  LR = lr_stat,
  df = df_diff,
  p_value = p_value
)

# Alternative: compare nested models with anova() if supported
# anova(m_null, m_ord)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. AIC/BIC for model comparison
# ------------------------------------------------------------

AIC(m_ord)
BIC(m_ord)

# compare with null model
AIC(m_null)
BIC(m_null)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Predicted category distribution
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Predicted probabilities per category for each observation
pred_prob <- predict(m_ord, newdata = dat, type = "prob")

# First few rows
head(pred_prob)

# Predicted class (most likely category)
pred_class <- predict(m_ord, newdata = dat, type = "class")

# Observed vs predicted table
obs_pred_tab <- table(
  Observed = dat$inter_zoning,
  Predicted = pred_class
)

obs_pred_tab

# Row-wise proportions of predicted categories
round(prop.table(obs_pred_tab, margin = 1), 3)

# Optional: summary of predicted probabilities by observed group
# This can be used to inspect calibration
dat_pred <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    predicted_class = pred_class
  ) %>%
  cbind(pred_prob)

head(dat_pred)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. If proportional odds assumption is violated:
#    Fit a generalized ordered logit model
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# The generalized ordered logit model allows the effect of a predictor
# to vary across the cutpoints (i.e., non-parallel slopes).
# Here, educ is allowed to have a different effect across thresholds:
m_gen <- clm(
  inter_zoning ~ educ,
  data = dat,
  link = "logit",
  nominal = ~ educ
)

summary(m_gen)

# Test whether the unrestricted (generalized) model is significantly better:
ll_ord <- as.numeric(logLik(m_ord))
ll_gen <- as.numeric(logLik(m_gen))

lr_gen <- 2 * (ll_gen - ll_ord)
df_gen <- attr(logLik(m_gen), "df") - attr(logLik(m_ord), "df")
p_gen <- pchisq(lr_gen, df = df_gen, lower.tail = FALSE)

data.frame(
  Model = "Generalized ordered logit vs ordered logit",
  LR = lr_gen,
  df = df_gen,
  p_value = p_gen
)

# An additional assumption check for a generalized model:
# nominal_test() tells you whether the non-parallel slope terms are needed
nominal_test(m_gen)

# If multiple predictors:
# m_gen_full <- clm(inter_zoning ~ educ + age_group + gender,
#                  data = dat, link = "logit",
#                  nominal = ~ educ + age_group)

# summary(m_gen_full)
# nominal_test(m_gen_full)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Alternative model if you want education as numeric rather than categorical
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# If education is truly ordinal but treated as numeric:
dat_num <- fisher_data %>%
  transmute(
    inter_zoning = as.integer(inter_zoning),
    educ_num = as.numeric(as.character(educ))
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(inter_zoning), !is.na(educ_num)) %>%
  mutate(inter_zoning = factor(inter_zoning, ordered = TRUE, levels = 1:10))

m_ord_num <- clm(inter_zoning ~ educ_num, data = dat_num, link = "logit")

summary(m_ord_num)
nominal_test(m_ord_num)

# LR test vs null
m_null_num <- clm(inter_zoning ~ 1, data = dat_num, link = "logit")
ll_null_num <- as.numeric(logLik(m_null_num))
ll_ord_num <- as.numeric(logLik(m_ord_num))
lr_num <- 2 * (ll_ord_num - ll_null_num)
df_num <- attr(logLik(m_ord_num), "df") - attr(logLik(m_null_num), "df")
p_num <- pchisq(lr_num, df = df_num, lower.tail = FALSE)

data.frame(
  Model = "Ordered logit with numeric education",
  LR = lr_num,
  df = df_num,
  p_value = p_num
)

AIC(m_ord_num)
BIC(m_ord_num)
